access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (dress research for the 1812 scene). British. A very dark brown-black wool double-breasted tailcoat cut square across the waist with tails to the knee, a turned-down collar and covered buttons; black wool knee breeches with a fall front and buttoned knee bands.
note: Proposed for the 1812 dress reference sets; not a Chicago or Fort Dearborn record. A museum garment: its record is typed by the museum photograph of it, as met_ci_1833_tailcoat_and_trousers is. Recorded by the 1812 dress build (officers-traders group) from the T-3461 dress research (docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3461/dress.json new_sources).
what_it_supplies: the cut and cloth of a prosperous man's dark tailcoat and knee breeches of the 1810s
what_it_does_not_supply: an American or frontier merchant's dress (these are British)
